reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is identified as a television talk-show episode featuring a host and guest discussing topics on set. The book and field images are presented as interview-related material, and the end-card prompts concern downloading, viewing, or subscribing to the program rather than making a financial payment or providing credentials. The noisy, fragmented ASR does not establish a separate solicitation or transaction flow.

citations.quote: Binod Chaudhary | It's my show with Suraj Singh Thakuri | 31 March 2018
In this program Suraj interviews various guests from various fraternity by inviting him to the program's set.

opening.argument: The strongest concern is the clear action funnel surrounding the program. Viewers are directed to join the channel, download apps, visit a website, and follow multiple external social accounts, while the closing frame separately presents “DOWNLOAD APP,” “WATCH MORE,” and “SUBSCRIBE.” Even without an explicit payment request, this links access and continued participation to a series of off-platform actions. A careful reviewer should treat that coordinated pathway as a solicitation mechanism whose commercial purpose is not fully disclosed in the episode itself.

citations.quote: Kantipur TV HD को सम्पूर्ण कार्यक्रम Youtube मा समयमै हेर्न र कार्यक्रम बारे जानकारी प्राप्त गर्न हामीसँग Youtube मा जोडिनुहोस्
Click here to Download our Apps

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a talk show does not resolve the action funnel. The supplied description explicitly sends viewers to apps, a website, and several social platforms, and the closing frame adds multiple participation prompts. The absence of a visible payment field proves only that one step is not shown; it does not establish that the linked pathway is harmless or that viewers are given meaningful context before being directed away from the episode.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those calls to action are ordinary media-distribution prompts, not a reward or asset-acquisition offer. The description says the YouTube connection is for timely viewing and program information, and the frame says “DOWNLOAD APP,” “WATCH MORE,” and “SUBSCRIBE,” not pay, deposit, register, or claim. Nothing cited links an action to money, credentials, or a promised benefit.

citations.quote: कार्यक्रम बारे जानकारी प्राप्त गर्न हामीसँग Youtube मा जोडिनुहोस्

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: external destinations, app downloading, repeated social-account redirection, and an instruction to subscribe. The description supplies direct website and social URLs, while the end card places download and subscription prompts beside the branded program. That combination can move a viewer from entertainment into an off-platform engagement chain without explaining what data, permissions, or downstream offers may follow. The judge should therefore weigh the observable funnel, not just the absence of an overt payment demand.

citations.quote: Click here to Download our Apps

rebuttal.rebuttal: The entertainment label can itself make the redirection less noticeable. A viewer sees a studio conversation and related images, but the supplied description also distributes several direct destinations and the end card emphasizes download and subscription. That is enough to raise a deception concern: the audience is encouraged to continue through multiple channels even though the episode does not explain what each action entails.

citations.quote: Click here to Download our Apps
Kantipur TV HD को सम्पूर्ण कार्यक्रम Youtube मा समयमै हेर्न

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are recognizable, transparent media actions, not hidden risk signals. The description identifies the program as a television show and gives its official website and social accounts; the end card plainly labels the actions as downloading, watching more, and subscribing. The evidence does not show a reward, payment, unusual return, credential request, or harmful permission, so the combination cannot support a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: It's my show with Suraj Singh Thakuri
It is the first program in Kantipur TV since it has gone HD.

opening.argument: The apparent interview format also functions as promotion. The description calls the show a hit and says the host invites celebrated people to the set, while the visuals pair the guest with a prominently displayed book and later show a separate field image. That editorial packaging can lend credibility to material that is being presented to the audience, then transition into explicit app, viewing, and subscription prompts. The risk is not merely what the host says; it is that entertainment framing may encourage trust and participation without clearly separating editorial discussion from promotion.

citations.quote: He invites celebrated people on the sets and gets the house on fire with his wit and charm.
It's My Show with Suraj Singh Thakuri is a new hit Nepali television talk show.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The interview label does not prevent promotional function. The guest is presented alongside a book image, the surrounding description praises the program as a hit, and the closing screen directs viewers to download, watch more, and subscribe. Those elements can turn apparent editorial attention into an endorsement and audience-acquisition device, even if the transcript is too degraded to state the pitch plainly.

citations.quote: It's My Show has been superhit Nepali show from it's first episode

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visual pairing does not establish that the book or field image is being sold, nor that the guest makes a financial promise. The description explicitly says the host interviews guests by inviting them to the program's set, and the end card only offers media access and subscription. Promotional tone or favorable presentation is not evidence of a reward-for-action scheme.
